result:
I played all 24 months. The final net cost is **$695.2M**. All three training runs finished on time, every month of inference demand was fully served, and there were no penalties.

**Settlement**

| Item | $M |
|---|---|
| GPU purchases | 500.0 |
| Power | 142.8 |
| Cloud reservations | 262.6 |
| Spot | 29.8 |
| Unserved inference | 0 |
| Resale income | −116.0 |
| Remaining power obligations after month 23 | +49.2 |
| Value of GPUs still owned at month 24 | −173.2 |
| **Net cost** | **695.2** |

**Training runs**
- **Months 0–7:** 94.5 / 60
- **Months 8–15:** 158.5 / 140
- **Months 16–23:** 320 / 320, met in the last month with roughly 14 kH-months of capacity to spare.

**How it went**
- **Months 0–7:** I bought 20k gen-H GPUs at the start and signed 32 MW of extra power, which came online in month 6. Small spot purchases covered the gap until then. This ran the first window well over its target.
- **Months 8–15:** The second window had more capacity than it needed, so I sold 6k gen-H GPUs in months 8–9. Selling before the gen-N launch avoided the 40% price drop on gen H. I also signed 8 MW of power so the remaining fleet stayed powered after the original 16 MW contract ended in month 19.
- **Months 16–23:** I took three 6-month cloud reservations of 10 kH each, starting in months 16, 17 and 18. The last one was signed after the gen-N launch in month 17, at the 25% lower price. Spot purchases topped up the margin each month. I sold another 3k gen H in the final month when the extra capacity was no longer needed.
- **Gen N:** I didn't buy any. It launched in month 17, so it would only have arrived around month 20 and been used for about four months, which made it more expensive per unit of compute than reservations or spot.

**What cost money without helping**
- **Extra training in the first two windows:** about 53 kH-months beyond what the runs needed, because purchased GPUs and power arrived in large blocks.
- **Power after the game ends:** $49.2M is still owed on power contracts beyond month 23.
